title.zh: 卷十九 百官公卿表
title.en: Volume 19: Table of Nobility Ranks and Government Offices
title.raw: 卷十九 百官公卿表 Volume 19: Table of nobility ranks and government offices

sentences.zh: 師古曰：「漢制，三公號稱萬石，其俸月各三百五十斛穀。

translations.literal: Shigu says: "Under Han regulations, the Three Excellencies were styled as ten-thousand-shi officials; each received a monthly salary of 350 hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: As Master Shigu notes: "In Han administrative practice, the Three Excellencies were ranked as 'ten-thousand-shi' officials, each receiving 350 hu of grain per month.

sentences.zh: 其稱中二千石者月各百八十斛，二千石者百二十斛，比二千石者百斛，千石者九十斛，比千石者八十斛，六百石者七十斛，比六百石者六十斛，四百石者五十斛，比四百石者四十五斛，三百石者四十斛，比三百石者三十七斛，二百石者三十斛，比二百石者二十七斛，一百石者十六斛。」〉

translations.literal: Those called 'mid-2,000-shi' each received 180 hu monthly; 2,000-shi got 120 hu; rank-equivalent to 2,000-shi got 100 hu; 1,000-shi got 90 hu; rank-equivalent to 1,000-shi got 80 hu; 600-shi got 70 hu; rank-equivalent to 600-shi got 60 hu; 400-shi got 50 hu; rank-equivalent to 400-shi got 45 hu; 300-shi got 40 hu; rank-equivalent to 300-shi got 37 hu; 200-shi got 30 hu; rank-equivalent to 200-shi got 27 hu; 100-shi got 16 hu."
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the 'middle 2,000-shi' class received 180 hu a month; the 2,000-shi class received 120; those equivalent to 2,000-shi received 100; the 1,000-shi class received 90; those equivalent to 1,000-shi received 80; the 600-shi class received 70; equivalents to 600-shi received 60; the 400-shi class received 50; equivalents to 400-shi received 45; the 300-shi class received 40; equivalents to 300-shi received 37; the 200-shi class received 30; equivalents to 200-shi received 27; and the 100-shi class received 16."

sentences.zh: 易敘宓羲、神農、黃帝作敎化民，[1]而傳述其官，[2]以為宓羲龍師名官，[3]神農火師火名，[4]黃帝雲師雲名，[5]少昊鳥師鳥名。

translations.literal: The Changes narrates how Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor established teachings to transform the people, and transmits accounts of their offices: in Fuxi's case, officials were named by dragon-masters; in Shennong's case, by fire-masters and fire names; in the Yellow Emperor's case, by cloud-masters and cloud names; and in Shaohao's case, by bird-masters and bird names.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes recounts that Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor instituted civilizing instruction for the people, and it also preserves their official nomenclature: Fuxi named offices after dragons, Shennong after fire, the Yellow Emperor after clouds, and Shaohao after birds.

sentences.zh: [6]自顓頊以來，為民師而命以民事，[7]有重黎、句芒、祝融、后土、蓐收、玄冥之官，然已上矣。

translations.literal: From Zhuanxu onward, they served as teachers of the people and were appointed to the people's affairs; there were offices of Chongli, Goumang, Zhurong, Houtu, Rushou, and Xuanming, but that already belongs to high antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of Zhuanxu onward, rulers made teachers of the people and charged officials with civil affairs. Posts such as Chongli, Goumang, Zhurong, Houtu, Rushou, and Xuanming belonged to that remote antiquity.

sentences.zh: [8]書載唐虞之際，命羲和四子[9]順天文，授民時；

translations.literal: The Documents records that in the age of Tang and Yu, the four sons of Xi and He were ordered to align with heavenly patterns and provide the people with the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says that in the era of Yao and Shun, the four sons of Xi and He were charged with observing the heavens and issuing the calendar to the people;

sentences.zh: 咨四岳，以舉賢材，揚側陋；

translations.literal: the Four Peaks were consulted in order to recommend worthy talent and raise those from obscure and humble positions;
translations.idiomatic: the Four Peaks were consulted so that worthy men might be recommended and the neglected and obscure brought forward;

sentences.zh: [10]十有二牧，柔遠能邇；

translations.literal: the twelve pastors were established, to bring distant peoples to compliance and make nearby peoples capable;
translations.idiomatic: the Twelve Governors were put in place, to pacify those far away and properly order those near at hand;

sentences.zh: [11]禹作司空，平水土；

translations.literal: Yu served as Minister of Works, leveling waters and lands;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was appointed Minister of Works to regulate the waters and set the land in order;

sentences.zh: [12]棄作后稷，播百穀；

translations.literal: Qi served as Houji, sowing the hundred grains;
translations.idiomatic: Qi was made Lord Millet and spread the cultivation of all the staple grains;

sentences.zh: [13]禼作司徒，敷五敎；

translations.literal: Xie served as Minister of Education, promulgating the Five Teachings;
translations.idiomatic: Xie was appointed Minister of Education and disseminated the Five Teachings;

sentences.zh: [14]咎繇作士，正五刑；

translations.literal: Gaoyao served as Minister of Justice, rectifying the five punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyao was made Minister of Justice and regularized the Five Punishments;

sentences.zh: [15]垂作共工，利器用；

translations.literal: Chui was appointed Gong Gong, to improve tools and implements;
translations.idiomatic: Chui was made Gong Gong, charged with improving tools and implements;

sentences.zh: [16]益作朕虞，育草木鳥獸；

translations.literal: Yi was appointed Imperial Forester, nurturing grasses, trees, birds, and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: Yi was appointed Imperial Forester, to cultivate grasses and trees and oversee birds and beasts;

sentences.zh: [17]伯夷作秩宗，典三禮；

translations.literal: Bo Yi served as Minister of Rites, administering the three rites;
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi was made Minister of Rites, in charge of the three ritual codes;

sentences.zh: [18]夔典樂，和神人；

translations.literal: Kui administered music, harmonizing spirits and men;
translations.idiomatic: Kui took charge of music, bringing gods and men into harmony;

sentences.zh: [19]龍作納言，出入帝命。

translations.literal: Long served as Receiver of Words, conveying in and out the emperor's commands.
translations.idiomatic: Long served as Receiver of Words, transmitting imperial commands to and from the throne.

sentences.zh: [20]夏、殷亡聞焉，[21]周官則備矣。

translations.literal: Of Xia and Shang there is no clear record heard, but the Zhou offices were complete.
translations.idiomatic: For the Xia and Shang we have no full account, but under Zhou the official system was complete.

sentences.zh: [22]天官冢宰，地官司徒，春官宗伯，夏官司馬，秋官司冦，冬官司空，是為六卿，[23]各有徒屬職分，用於百事。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Office was the Grand Steward, the Earthly Office the Minister of Education, the Spring Office the Minister of Rites, the Summer Office the Minister of War, the Autumn Office the Minister of Justice, and the Winter Office the Minister of Works; these were the Six Ministers. Each had subordinates and assigned duties, applied in the hundred affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou system set out six chief ministries: the Heavenly Office under the Grand Steward, the Earthly under the Minister of Education, the Spring under the Minister of Rites, the Summer under the Minister of War, the Autumn under the Minister of Justice, and the Winter under the Minister of Works. Together these formed the Six Ministers, each with subordinate officials and defined duties for the full range of state business.

sentences.zh: [24]太師、太傅、太保，是為三公，[25]蓋參天子，坐而議政，無不緫統，故不以一職為官名。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector were the Three Excellencies. They assisted the Son of Heaven, sat in council on government, and oversaw all matters in general; therefore they were not named for any single office.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector constituted the Three Excellencies. They stood alongside the Son of Heaven in governing, deliberated policy in council, and oversaw all administration. For that reason, their titles were not tied to a single bureau.

sentences.zh: 又立三少為之副，少師、少傅、少保，是為孤卿，與六卿為九焉。

translations.literal: There were also established three Juniors as their deputies - Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector; these were the Solitary Ministers, and with the Six Ministers made nine.
translations.idiomatic: Three junior counterparts were also established as their deputies: Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector. These were called the Solitary Ministers, bringing the total with the Six Ministers to nine.

sentences.zh: 記曰三公無官，言有其人然后充之，[26]舜之於堯，伊尹於湯，周公、召公於周，是也。

translations.literal: The Record says, "The Three Excellencies have no fixed office," meaning that only when there are the right men are those posts filled: Shun under Yao, yiyin day under Tang, and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao under Zhou are examples.
translations.idiomatic: As the Record puts it, "The Three Excellencies are not fixed offices" - meaning the rank exists only when a person worthy of it appears. Shun serving Yao, yiyin day serving Tang, and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao under Zhou are classic examples.

sentences.zh: 或說司馬主天，司徒主人，司空主土，是為三公。

translations.literal: Some explanations say the Minister of War governed Heaven, the Minister of Education governed Man, and the Minister of Works governed Earth; these were the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Another interpretation holds that the Minister of War corresponded to Heaven, the Minister of Education to Humanity, and the Minister of Works to Earth - and that these formed the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 四岳謂四方諸侯。

translations.literal: The Four Peaks refers to the feudal lords of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: "Four Peaks" means the regional lords of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 自周衰，官失而百職亂，戰國並爭，各變異。

translations.literal: From the decline of Zhou onward, offices were lost and the hundred functions fell into disorder; the Warring States contended together, each making changes and differences.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou declined, offices lost their proper form and the full administrative order broke down. As the Warring States fought for supremacy, each state altered the system in its own way.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，建皇帝之號，立百官之職。

translations.literal: When Qin unified all under Heaven, it established the title of Emperor and set up the offices of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin unified the realm, it instituted the imperial title and established the full framework of official posts.

sentences.zh: 漢因循而不革，明簡易，隨時宜也。

translations.literal: Han followed what had been transmitted and did not radically alter it, making it clear, simple, and easy, adapting to what was suitable for the times.
translations.idiomatic: The Han largely continued this framework rather than overhauling it, favoring clear and simple arrangements suited to contemporary needs.

sentences.zh: 其後頗有所改。

translations.literal: Afterward there were, in some measure, changes.
translations.idiomatic: Later on, however, a number of revisions were introduced.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，慕從古官，而吏民弗安，亦多虐政，遂以亂亡。

translations.literal: Wang Mang usurped the throne, admired and followed ancient offices, yet officials and people were not at ease, and there were many cruel policies; thus through disorder it perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized the throne, he tried to imitate archaic institutions. But officials and commoners alike found no stability under them, harsh governance multiplied, and his regime collapsed in disorder.

sentences.zh: 故略表舉大分，[29]以通古今，備溫故知新之義云。

translations.literal: Therefore this table briefly presents and raises the major divisions, in order to connect antiquity and the present, and to complete the meaning of reviewing the old to know the new.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason, this table sets out the main institutional divisions in summary form, linking ancient and later practice and fulfilling the principle that by reviewing the old, one comes to understand the new.

sentences.zh: 相國、丞相，皆秦官，金印紫綬，掌丞天子助理萬機。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State and the Grand Chancellor were both Qin offices. They bore gold seals with purple ribbons and were responsible for assisting the Son of Heaven in managing all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State and the Grand Chancellor were both Qin offices, bearing gold seals with purple ribbons. They were charged with assisting the Son of Heaven in managing all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 秦有左右，高帝即位，置一丞相，十一年更名相國，綠綬。

translations.literal: Qin had both a Left and Right Chancellor. When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he established a single Grand Chancellor. In the eleventh year the title was changed to Chancellor of State, with a green ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin there were both Left and Right Chancellors. When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he appointed a single Grand Chancellor. In the eleventh year, the title was changed to Chancellor of State, with a green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 孝惠、高后置左右丞相，文帝一年復置一丞相。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui and Empress Dowager Gao, Left and Right Grand Chancellors were established. In the first year of Emperor Wen, a single Grand Chancellor was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui and Empress Dowager Gao, Left and Right Grand Chancellors were appointed. In the first year of Emperor Wen, a single Grand Chancellor was restored.

sentences.zh: 有兩長史，秩千石。

translations.literal: There were two Chief Clerks, with a salary rank of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The office had two Chief Clerks, each ranked at one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽二年更名大司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai, the title was changed to Grand Minister of Education
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai, the title was changed to Grand Minister of Education

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩五年初置司直，秩比二千石，掌佐丞相舉不法。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, the office of Chancellor's Rectifier was first established, with a salary rank equivalent to two thousand shi, responsible for assisting the Grand Chancellor in exposing lawbreakers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, the Chancellor's Rectifier was first established at a rank equivalent to two thousand shi, charged with assisting the Grand Chancellor in exposing illegality.

sentences.zh: 太尉，秦官，金印紫綬，掌武事。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant was a Qin office, bearing a gold seal with purple ribbon, responsible for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant was a Qin office, bearing a gold seal with purple ribbon, in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 武帝建元二年省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 元狩四年初置大司馬，以冠將軍之號。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanshou, the title Grand Marshal was first established, placed above the General's title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanshou, the title Grand Marshal was first established as a prefix to the General's title.

sentences.zh: 宣帝地節三年置大司馬，不冠將軍，亦無印綬官屬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dijie under Emperor Xuan, a Grand Marshal was appointed without the General's prefix and without seal, ribbon, or subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Dijie 3 under Emperor Xuan, a Grand Marshal was appointed without the General prefix and without seal, ribbon, or subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 成帝綏和元年初賜大司馬金印紫綬，置官屬，祿比丞相，去將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Suihe under Emperor Cheng, the Grand Marshal was granted a gold seal with purple ribbon, given subordinate officials, a salary equal to the Grand Chancellor's, and the General title was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Suihe 1 under Emperor Cheng, the Grand Marshal was granted a gold seal with purple ribbon, given subordinate staff, a salary matching the Grand Chancellor's, and the General title was dropped.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平二年復去大司馬印綬、官屬，冠將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianping under Emperor Ai, the Grand Marshal's seal, ribbon, and subordinate officials were removed again, and the General title was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianping 2 under Emperor Ai, the Grand Marshal's seal, ribbon, and staff were again removed, and the General prefix was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 元壽二年復賜大司馬印綬，置官屬，去將軍，位在司徒上。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou, the Grand Marshal was again granted a seal and ribbon, given subordinate officials, the General title was removed, and his position was placed above the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou, the Grand Marshal was again granted seal and ribbon, given subordinate staff, the General title dropped, and his rank placed above the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 有長史，秩千石。

translations.literal: They had Chief Clerks, rank 1,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Each office included a Chief Clerk of 1,000-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫，秦官，位上卿，銀印青綬，掌副丞相。

translations.literal: The Grandee Secretary was a Qin office, ranked among the senior ministers, bearing a silver seal with blue-green ribbon, responsible for serving as the deputy of the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grandee Secretary was a Qin office ranked among the senior ministers, bearing a silver seal with blue-green ribbon, serving as deputy to the Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 有兩丞，秩千石。

translations.literal: There were two Deputies, with a salary rank of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The office had two Deputies, each ranked at one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 一曰中丞，在殿中蘭臺，掌圖籍祕書，外督部刺史，內領侍御史員十五人，受公卿奏事，舉劾按章。

translations.literal: One was called the Palace Deputy, stationed in the Orchid Terrace within the palace halls, responsible for maps, registers, and secret documents. Externally he supervised the Regional Inspectors; internally he commanded the fifteen Attendant Censors, received memorials from the ministers, and conducted impeachments and investigations.
translations.idiomatic: One was called the Palace Deputy, stationed at the Orchid Terrace within the palace. He oversaw maps, registers, and secret documents. Externally, he supervised the Regional Inspectors; internally, he commanded the fifteen Attendant Censors, received memorials from the ministers, and conducted impeachments and investigations.

sentences.zh: 成帝綏和元年更名大司空，祿比丞相，置長史如中丞，官職如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Suihe under Emperor Cheng, the title was changed to Grand Minister of Works, with salary equal to the Grand Chancellor, a Chief Clerk appointed like the Central Censor, and duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Suihe 1 under Emperor Cheng, the title was changed to Grand Minister of Works, with salary matching the Grand Chancellor, a Chief Clerk like the Central Censor, and duties otherwise unchanged.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平二年復爲御史大夫，元壽二年復爲大司空，御史中丞更名御史長史。

translations.literal: In Jianping 2 under Emperor Ai, the title was restored to Grandee Secretary. In the second year of Yuanshou, it was changed back to Grand Minister of Works, and the Palace Deputy was renamed Chief Clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianping 2 under Emperor Ai, the title reverted to Grandee Secretary. In the second year of Yuanshou, it was changed back to Grand Minister of Works, and the Palace Deputy was renamed Chief Clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 侍御史有繡衣直指，出討姦猾，治大獄，武帝所制，不常置。

translations.literal: Among the Attendant Censors there was the Embroidered Garment Direct Appointee, dispatched to suppress crafty and treacherous individuals and to handle major legal cases. This was instituted by Emperor Wu and was not a permanent position.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Attendant Censors was the Embroidered Garment Direct Appointee, sent out to suppress treachery and manage major cases. This was a creation of Emperor Wu and not a permanent position.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 30.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 30.

sentences.zh: 太傅，古官，高后元年初置，金印紫綬。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor was an ancient office; it was first established in the first year of Empress Gao, with gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor was an ancient office. It was first instituted in Empress Gao's first year, with the insignia of a gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後省，八年復置。

translations.literal: Later it was abolished; in year eight it was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: The office was later abolished, then restored in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 後省，哀帝元壽二年復置。

translations.literal: Later it was abolished; in Emperor Ai's Yuanshou second year it was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: It was again abolished, then restored in the second year of Emperor Ai's Yuanshou era.

sentences.zh: 位在三公上。

translations.literal: Its rank was above the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Its precedence stood above that of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太師、太保，皆古官，平帝元始元年皆初置，金印紫綬。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor and Grand Protector were both ancient offices; both were first established in Emperor Ping's Yuanshi first year, with gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The offices of Grand Preceptor and Grand Protector were both ancient in origin. Both were first instituted in Emperor Ping's Yuanshi first year, bearing the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 太師位在太傅上，太保次太傅。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor ranked above the Grand Tutor; the Grand Protector ranked next to the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor ranked above the Grand Tutor, while the Grand Protector ranked just below him.

sentences.zh: 前後左右將軍，皆周末官，秦因之，位上卿，金印紫綬。

translations.literal: The Generals of the Van, Rear, Left, and Right were all late-Zhou offices; Qin continued them. Their rank was Senior Minister, with gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The Generals of the Van, Rear, Left, and Right all originated in the late Zhou and were retained by Qin. They held senior-minister rank, marked by a gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 漢不常置，或有前後，或有左右，皆掌兵及四夷。

translations.literal: Han did not maintain them constantly; sometimes there were Van and Rear, sometimes Left and Right. All managed troops and the Four Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Han did not keep these commands as fixed offices: at times there were Generals of the Van and Rear, at times of the Left and Right. In all cases, they commanded troops and handled affairs involving the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 有長史，秩千石。

translations.literal: They had Chief Clerks, rank 1,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Each office included a Chief Clerk of 1,000-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 奉常，秦官，掌宗廟禮儀，有丞。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies was a Qin office, responsible for ancestral temple rites and ceremonies, with a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies was a Qin office in charge of ancestral temple rites and ceremonies, with a Deputy.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名太常。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the middle reign period under Emperor Jing, the title was changed to Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth middle year of Emperor Jing's reign, the title was changed to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 屬官有太樂、太祝、太宰、太史、太卜、太醫六令丞，又均官、都水兩長丞，又諸廟寢園食官令長丞，有廱太宰、太祝令丞，五畤各一尉。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included six Directors and Deputies: Grand Music, Grand Invocator, Grand Steward, Grand Astrologer, Grand Diviner, and Grand Physician. There were also two Chiefs and Deputies: the Equalization Office and the Capital Water Office. Further, there were Directors, Chiefs, and Deputies for the various temple chambers, park provisioning offices, and the Grand Steward and Grand Invocator of Yong, with one Commandant for each of the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included six Directors and Deputies — Grand Music, Grand Invocator, Grand Steward, Grand Astrologer, Grand Diviner, and Grand Physician. Additionally, the Equalization Office and Capital Water Office each had a Chief and Deputy. There were also Directors and Deputies for the temple chambers, park provisions, and the Yong Grand Steward and Grand Invocator, with one Commandant for each of the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: 又博士及諸陵縣皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The Erudites and all the imperial mausoleum counties were also under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Erudites and all the imperial mausoleum counties also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名太祝爲祠祀，武帝太初元年更曰廟祀，初置太卜。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the Grand Invocator was renamed the Sacrificial Worship Director. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it was renamed the Temple Worship Director, and the Grand Diviner was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the Grand Invocator was renamed Director of Sacrificial Worship. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it became the Director of Temple Worship, and the Grand Diviner was first established.

sentences.zh: 博士，秦官，掌通古今，秩比六百石，員多至數十人。

translations.literal: The Erudites were a Qin office, responsible for expertise in ancient and modern affairs, ranked at the equivalent of six hundred shi, with a complement rising to several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: The Erudites were a Qin office responsible for mastery of ancient and modern learning, ranked at the equivalent of six hundred shi. Their number sometimes reached several dozen.

sentences.zh: 武帝建元五年初置五經博士，宣帝黃龍元年稍增員十二人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, the Erudites of the Five Classics were first established. In Huanglong 1 under Emperor Xuan, the complement was gradually increased to twelve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, the Erudites of the Five Classics were first established. In Huanglong 1 under Emperor Xuan, their number was gradually increased to twelve.

sentences.zh: 元帝永光元年分諸陵邑屬三輔。

translations.literal: In Yongguang 1 under Emperor Yuan, the various mausoleum towns were separated and placed under the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongguang 1 under Emperor Yuan, the mausoleum towns were transferred to the jurisdiction of the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 王莽改太常曰「秩宗」。

translations.literal: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Master of Ceremonies to "Director of Ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Master of Ceremonies to "Director of Ranks."

sentences.zh: 郎中令，秦官，掌宮殿掖門戶，有丞。

translations.literal: The Director of the Gentlemen of the Palace was a Qin office, responsible for the palace halls and side gates, with a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Gentlemen of the Palace was a Qin office in charge of the palace halls and side gates, with a Deputy.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名光祿勳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the title was changed to Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the title was changed to Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 屬官有大夫、郎、謁者，皆秦官。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials included the Grandees, Gentlemen, and Ushers, all Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included the Grandees, Gentlemen, and Ushers — all Qin offices.

sentences.zh: 又期門、羽林皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The Gate Guards and the Feathered Forest also fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Guards and the Feathered Forest Guards also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 大夫掌論議，有太中大夫、中大夫、諫大夫，皆無員，多至數十人。

translations.literal: The Grandees were responsible for deliberation and discussion. There were Grand Palace Grandees, Palace Grandees, and Remonstrant Grandees — all without a fixed complement, sometimes numbering several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: The Grandees were responsible for deliberation and debate. They comprised Grand Palace Grandees, Palace Grandees, and Remonstrant Grandees, with no fixed complement — sometimes numbering several dozen.

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩五年初置諫大夫，秩比八百石，太初元年更名中大夫爲光祿大夫，秩比二千石，太中大夫秩比千石如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, the Remonstrant Grandee was first established at the equivalent of eight hundred shi. In the first year of Taichu, the Palace Grandee was renamed Grandee of the Glorious Emolument at the equivalent of two thousand shi; the Grand Palace Grandee remained at the equivalent of one thousand shi as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, the Remonstrant Grandee was first established at an equivalent rank of eight hundred shi. In the first year of Taichu, the Palace Grandee was renamed Grandee of the Glorious Emolument at two thousand shi; the Grand Palace Grandee remained at one thousand shi as before.

sentences.zh: 郎掌守門戶，出充車騎，有議郎、中郎、侍郎、郎中，皆無員，多至千人。

translations.literal: The Gentlemen were responsible for guarding the gates and, when dispatched, serving as chariot and cavalry escorts. They comprised Consultant Gentlemen, Palace Gentlemen, Attendant Gentlemen, and Gentlemen of the Palace, all without a fixed complement — sometimes numbering up to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Gentlemen guarded the gates and, when dispatched, served as chariot and cavalry escorts. They comprised Consultant Gentlemen, Palace Gentlemen, Attendant Gentlemen, and Gentlemen of the Palace — with no fixed complement, sometimes numbering up to a thousand.

sentences.zh: 議郎、中郎秩比六百石，侍郎比四百石，郎中比三百石。

translations.literal: Consultant Gentlemen and Palace Gentlemen were ranked at the equivalent of six hundred shi; Attendant Gentlemen at four hundred shi; and Gentlemen of the Palace at three hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Consultant Gentlemen and Palace Gentlemen ranked at the equivalent of six hundred shi, Attendant Gentlemen at four hundred, and Gentlemen of the Palace at three hundred.

sentences.zh: 中郎有五官、左、右三將，秩皆比二千石。

translations.literal: The Palace Gentlemen had three Commanders: the Five Offices, Left, and Right, all ranked at the equivalent of two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Gentlemen had three Commanders — Five Offices, Left, and Right — each ranked at the equivalent of two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 郎中有車、戶、騎三將，秩皆比千石。

translations.literal: The Gentlemen of the Palace had three Commanders: Chariot, Gate, and Cavalry, all ranked at the equivalent of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Gentlemen of the Palace had three Commanders — Chariot, Gate, and Cavalry — each ranked at the equivalent of one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 謁者掌賔讚受事，員七十人，秩比六百石，有僕射，秩比千石。

translations.literal: The Ushers were responsible for receiving guests, assisting in ceremonies, and handling affairs. Their complement was seventy, ranked at the equivalent of six hundred shi, with a Chief Usher ranked at the equivalent of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Ushers received guests, assisted in ceremonies, and handled affairs. Their complement was seventy, ranked at six hundred shi, with a Chief Usher ranked at one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 期門掌執兵送從，武帝建元三年初置，比郎，無員，多至千人，有僕射，秩比千石。

translations.literal: The Gate Guards were responsible for bearing arms and providing escort. First established in the third year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, they ranked equivalent to Gentlemen, had no fixed complement (sometimes reaching a thousand), with a Chief ranked at one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Guards bore arms and provided escort. First established in the third year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, they ranked equivalent to Gentlemen, with no fixed complement — sometimes reaching a thousand — and a Chief ranked at one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始元年更名虎賁郎，置中郎將，秩比二千石。

translations.literal: In Yuanshi 1 under Emperor Ping, they were renamed Tiger-Ben Gentlemen, and a Commander of the Palace Gentlemen was established at the equivalent of two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanshi 1 under Emperor Ping, they were renamed Tiger-Ben Gentlemen, with a Commander ranked at two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 羽林掌送從，次期門，武帝太初元年初置，名曰建章營騎，後更名羽林騎。

translations.literal: The Feathered Forest Guards provided escort, ranking below the Gate Guards. First established in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, they were originally named the Jianzhang Camp Cavalry, later renamed the Feathered Forest Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Feathered Forest Guards provided escort, ranking below the Gate Guards. First established in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu as the Jianzhang Camp Cavalry, they were later renamed the Feathered Forest Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又取從軍死事之子孫養羽林，官敎以五兵，號曰羽林孤兒。

translations.literal: Additionally, the sons and grandsons of soldiers who died in battle were taken and raised in the Feathered Forest, where they were officially trained in the five weapons. They were called the 'Feathered Forest Orphans.'
translations.idiomatic: Additionally, the sons and grandsons of soldiers killed in battle were adopted into the Feathered Forest and trained in the five weapons. They were known as the 'Feathered Forest Orphans.'

sentences.zh: 羽林有令丞。

translations.literal: The Feathered Forest had a Director and Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Feathered Forest had a Director and a Deputy.

sentences.zh: 宣帝令中郎將、騎都尉監羽林，秩比二千石。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan decreed that the Commander of the Palace Gentlemen and the Cavalry Commandant should supervise the Feathered Forest, at a rank equivalent to two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan appointed the Commander of the Palace Gentlemen and the Cavalry Commandant to oversee the Feathered Forest, each ranked at two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 僕射，秦官，自侍中、尚書、博士、郎皆有。

translations.literal: The Chief was a Qin office; the Attendants-in-Ordinary, Masters of Documents, Erudites, and Gentlemen all had one.
translations.idiomatic: The title of Chief was a Qin institution. The Attendants-in-Ordinary, Masters of Documents, Erudites, and Gentlemen all had one.

sentences.zh: 古者重武官，有主射以督課之，軍屯吏、騶、宰、永巷宮人皆有，取其領事之號。

translations.literal: In ancient times military officials were esteemed, and there was a Master of Archery to supervise and assess them. Military garrison clerks, outriders, stewards, and the personnel of the Eternal Lane all had one, taking the title from its supervisory function.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, military officials were highly valued, with a Master of Archery to supervise and assess them. Military garrison clerks, outriders, stewards, and Eternal Lane palace staff all had such a post, the title deriving from its supervisory function.

sentences.zh: 衞尉，秦官，掌宮門衞屯兵，有丞。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guards was a Qin office, responsible for the palace gate guards and garrison troops, with a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Guards was a Qin office in charge of the palace gate guards and garrison troops, with a Deputy.

sentences.zh: 景帝初更名中大夫令，後元年復爲衞尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jing's reign, the title was changed to Director of the Palace Grandees. In the first year of the Later period, it was restored to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Jing's reign, the title was changed to Director of the Palace Grandees. In the first year of the Later period, it was restored to Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 屬官有公車司馬、衞士、旅賁三令丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included three Directors and Deputies: the Public Carriage Commandant, the Guard Soldiers, and the Traveling Warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included three Directors and Deputies: the Public Carriage Commandant, the Guard Soldiers, and the Traveling Warriors.

sentences.zh: 衞士三丞。

translations.literal: The Guard Soldiers had three Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Guard Soldiers office had three Deputies.

sentences.zh: 又諸屯衞候、司馬二十二官皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Additionally, the various garrison guards, commandants, and marshals — twenty-two offices in all — were all under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Additionally, all twenty-two garrison guard and marshal offices fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 長樂、建章、甘泉衞尉皆掌其宮，職略同，不常置。

translations.literal: The Commandants of the Guards for the Changle, Jianzhang, and Ganquan palaces each oversaw their respective palaces, with duties broadly similar, and were not permanently maintained.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandants of the Guards for the Changle, Jianzhang, and Ganquan palaces each oversaw their respective palaces. Their duties were broadly similar, and the positions were not permanent.

sentences.zh: 太僕，秦官，掌輿馬，有兩丞。

translations.literal: The Grand Coachman was a Qin office, responsible for carriages and horses, with two Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Coachman was a Qin office in charge of carriages and horses, with two Deputies.

sentences.zh: 屬官有大廄、未央、家馬三令，各五丞一尉。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included three Directors: the Grand Stables, the Weiyang Stables, and the Imperial Stables, each with five Deputies and one Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included three Directors — Grand Stables, Weiyang Stables, and Imperial Stables — each with five Deputies and one Commandant.

sentences.zh: 又車府、路軨、騎馬、駿馬四令丞；

translations.literal: Also four Directors and Deputies: the Carriage Office, Road Carriages, Riding Horses, and Fine Horses;
translations.idiomatic: Additionally, four Directors and Deputies: the Carriage Office, Road Carriages, Riding Horses, and Fine Horses;

sentences.zh: 又龍馬、閑駒、橐泉、騊駼、承華五監長丞；

translations.literal: also five Supervisors and Chiefs with Deputies: Dragon Horses, Idle Colts, Tuoquan, Taotu, and Chenghua;
translations.idiomatic: five Supervisors with Chiefs and Deputies: Dragon Horses, Idle Colts, Tuoquan, Taotu, and Chenghua;

sentences.zh: 又邊郡六牧師菀令，各三丞；

translations.literal: also six Pasture Park Directors in the border commanderies, each with three Deputies;
translations.idiomatic: six Pasture Park Directors in the border commanderies, each with three Deputies;

sentences.zh: 又牧橐、昆蹏令丞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Also the Directors and Deputies of the Camel Pasture and Kunti all fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Directors and Deputies of the Camel Pasture and Kunti also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 中太僕掌皇太后輿馬，不常置也。

translations.literal: The Palace Grand Coachman oversaw the carriages and horses of the Empress Dowager; the position was not permanent.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Grand Coachman oversaw the Empress Dowager's carriages and horses. The position was not permanent.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名家馬爲挏馬，初置路軨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Imperial Stables were renamed the Fermented Mare's Milk Stables, and the Road Carriages office was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Imperial Stables were renamed the Kumiss Stables, and the Road Carriages office was first established.

sentences.zh: 廷尉，秦官，[59]掌刑辟，有正、左右監，秩皆千石。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice was a Qin office; it managed punishments and penal law, and had an Adjudicator and Left and Right Supervisors, all rank 1,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice was a Qin institution. It oversaw criminal law and punishments, and included a principal adjudicator plus left and right supervisors, all at 1,000-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名大理，武帝建元四年復為廷尉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year it was renamed Grand Judge; in Emperor Wu's Jianyuan fourth year it returned to Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year, the office was renamed Grand Judge; in Emperor Wu's fourth Jianyuan year, it reverted to Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 宣帝地節三年初置左右平，秩皆六百石。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuan's Dijie third year, Left and Right Arbiters were first established, all rank 600 shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Xuan's Dijie era, the offices of Left and Right Arbiter were first created, each at 600-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽二年復為大理。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ai's Yuanshou second year it again became Grand Judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ai's Yuanshou era, it was once more renamed Grand Judge.

sentences.zh: 王莽改曰作士。

translations.literal: Wang Mang changed its name to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang renamed the office as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 典客，秦官，掌諸歸義蠻夷，有丞。

translations.literal: The Director of Guests was a Qin office, responsible for all the submitted barbarian peoples, with a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Guests was a Qin office in charge of the submitted barbarian peoples, with a Deputy.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名大行令，武帝太初元年更名大鴻臚。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the title was changed to Director of Grand Conduct. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it was changed to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, it was renamed Director of Grand Conduct. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it became the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 屬官有行人、譯官、別火三令丞及郡邸長丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included three Directors and Deputies: the Envoys, Interpreters, and Separate Fire, as well as the Chiefs and Deputies of the commandery lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included three Directors and Deputies — Envoys, Interpreters, and Separate Fire — as well as the Chiefs and Deputies of the commandery lodges.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名行人爲大行令，初置別火。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Envoys were renamed the Director of Grand Conduct, and the Separate Fire office was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Envoy office was renamed Director of Grand Conduct, and the Separate Fire office was first established.

sentences.zh: 王莽改大鴻臚曰典樂。

translations.literal: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Herald to Director of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Herald 'Director of Music.'

sentences.zh: 初，置郡國邸屬少府，中屬中尉，後屬大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Originally, the commandery and kingdom lodges were placed under the Privy Treasurer, then transferred to the Capital Commandant, and later placed under the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, the commandery and kingdom lodges fell under the Privy Treasurer, then were transferred to the Capital Commandant, and later placed under the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 宗正，秦官，[63]掌親屬，有丞。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan was a Qin office; it managed imperial kinship affairs and had a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Clan was a Qin institution responsible for matters of the ruling house's kinsmen, with a Deputy attached.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始四年更名宗伯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ping's Yuanshi fourth year, it was renamed Minister of the Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era, the office was renamed Minister of the Clan.

sentences.zh: 屬官有都司空令丞，內官長丞。

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices included Director and Deputy of the Metropolitan Works Office, and Chief and Deputy of the Inner Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate personnel included the Director and Deputy of the Metropolitan Works Office, as well as the Chief and Deputy of the Inner Offices.

sentences.zh: 又諸公主家令、門尉皆屬焉。

translations.literal: In addition, the Household Directors and Gate Commandants of all princess households were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: It also held authority over the Household Directors and Gate Commandants of all imperial princesses.

sentences.zh: 王莽并其官於秩宗。

translations.literal: Wang Mang merged this office into the Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang absorbed this office into the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，內官屬少府，中屬主爵，後屬宗正。

translations.literal: Originally, the Inner Offices belonged to the Privy Treasurer; in the middle period they belonged to the Commandant of Nobility Ranks; later they belonged to the Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Inner Offices were under the Privy Treasurer. In an intermediate period they were placed under the Commandant of Nobility Ranks, and later reassigned to the Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 治粟內史，秦官，掌穀貨，有兩丞。

translations.literal: The Internal Clerk for Grain was a Qin office, responsible for grain and commodities, with two Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Internal Clerk for Grain was a Qin office in charge of grain and commodities, with two Deputies.

sentences.zh: 景帝後元年更名大農令，武帝太初元年更名大司農。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Jing's Later period, the title was changed to Director of Grand Agriculture. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it was changed to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Jing's Later period, the title became Director of Grand Agriculture. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it became Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 屬官有太倉、均輸、平準、都內、籍田五令丞，斡官、鐵市兩長丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included five Directors and Deputies: Grand Granary, Equitable Transport, Price Stabilization, Capital Treasury, and Ritual Field; and two Chiefs and Deputies: the Monopoly Office and the Iron Market.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included five Directors and Deputies — Grand Granary, Equitable Transport, Price Stabilization, Capital Treasury, and Ritual Field — and two Chiefs and Deputies: the Monopoly Office and the Iron Market.

sentences.zh: 又郡國諸倉農監、都水六十五官長丞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Additionally, the various granaries, agricultural supervisors, and capital water officials of the commanderies and kingdoms — sixty-five Chiefs and Deputies in all — were all under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Additionally, all sixty-five Chiefs and Deputies of the commandery and kingdom granaries, agricultural supervisors, and water offices fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 騪粟都尉，武帝軍官，不常置。

translations.literal: The Grain Transport Commandant was a military office under Emperor Wu, not permanently maintained.
translations.idiomatic: The Grain Transport Commandant was a military office of Emperor Wu's era, not permanently maintained.

sentences.zh: 王莽改大司農曰羲和，後更爲納言。

translations.literal: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Minister of Agriculture to Xi He, and later changed it again to Receiver of Words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang renamed the Grand Minister of Agriculture 'Xi He,' later changing it again to 'Receiver of Words.'

sentences.zh: 初，斡官屬少府，中屬主爵，後屬大司農。

translations.literal: Originally, the Monopoly Office was under the Privy Treasurer, then transferred to the Director of Nobility Ranks, and later placed under the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, the Monopoly Office fell under the Privy Treasurer, then was transferred to the Director of Nobility Ranks, and later to the Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 少府，秦官，掌山海池澤之稅，以給共養，有六丞。

translations.literal: The Privy Treasurer was a Qin office, responsible for the taxes on mountains, seas, ponds, and marshes, used to supply the imperial household's needs, with six Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Treasurer was a Qin office in charge of taxes on mountains, seas, ponds, and marshlands, used to supply the imperial household. It had six Deputies.

sentences.zh: 屬官有尚書、符節、太醫、太官、湯官、導官、樂府、若盧、考工室、左弋、居室、甘泉居室、左右司空、東織、西織、東園匠十二官令丞，又胞人、都水、均官三長丞，又上林中十池監，又中書謁者、黃門、鉤盾、尚方、御府、永巷、內者、宦者七官令丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included twelve Directors and Deputies: the Masters of Documents, Tally and Credentials, Grand Physician, Grand Provisioner, Hot Water, Rice Processing, Music Bureau, Arsenal, Artisan Workshop, Left Archer, Dwelling Office, Ganquan Dwelling Office, Left and Right Ministers of Works, Eastern Weaving, Western Weaving, and Eastern Garden Artisans. There were also three Chiefs and Deputies: the Butchery, Capital Water, and Equalization offices. Additionally, the ten pond supervisors within the Shanglin Park, and seven Directors and Deputies: the Palace Secretary Ushers, Yellow Gate, Hook and Shield, Imperial Workshops, Imperial Wardrobe, Eternal Lane, Inner Attendants, and Eunuch Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included twelve Directors and Deputies — Masters of Documents, Tally and Credentials, Grand Physician, Grand Provisioner, Hot Water, Rice Processing, Music Bureau, Arsenal, Artisan Workshop, Left Archer, Dwelling Office, Ganquan Dwelling Office, Left and Right Ministers of Works, Eastern Weaving, Western Weaving, and Eastern Garden Artisans. Three Chiefs and Deputies: Butchery, Capital Water, and Equalization. Ten pond supervisors within the Shanglin Park. And seven Directors and Deputies: Palace Secretary Ushers, Yellow Gate, Hook and Shield, Imperial Workshops, Imperial Wardrobe, Eternal Lane, Inner Attendants, and Eunuch Attendants.

sentences.zh: 諸僕射、署長、中黃門皆屬焉。

translations.literal: All the Chiefs, Bureau Heads, and Palace Yellow Gate officials also fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: All the Chiefs, Bureau Heads, and Palace Yellow Gate officials also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名考工室爲考工，左弋爲佽飛，居室爲保宮，甘泉居室爲昆臺，永巷爲掖廷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Artisan Workshop was renamed the Artisans' Bureau, the Left Archer became the Swift Flyer, the Dwelling Office became the Palace Guardian, the Ganquan Dwelling Office became the Kunlun Terrace, and the Eternal Lane became the Lateral Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the names were changed: Artisan Workshop to Artisans' Bureau, Left Archer to Swift Flyer, Dwelling Office to Palace Guardian, Ganquan Dwelling to Kunlun Terrace, and Eternal Lane to Lateral Court.

sentences.zh: 佽飛掌弋射，有九丞兩尉，太官七丞，昆臺五丞，樂府三丞，掖廷八丞，宦者七丞，鉤盾五丞兩尉。

translations.literal: The Swift Flyer oversaw crossbow hunting, with nine Deputies and two Commandants. The Grand Provisioner had seven Deputies, the Kunlun Terrace five, the Music Bureau three, the Lateral Court eight, the Eunuch Attendants seven, and the Hook and Shield five Deputies and two Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: The Swift Flyer oversaw crossbow hunting, with nine Deputies and two Commandants. The Grand Provisioner had seven Deputies; the Kunlun Terrace, five; the Music Bureau, three; the Lateral Court, eight; the Eunuch Attendants, seven; and the Hook and Shield, five Deputies and two Commandants.

sentences.zh: 成帝建始四年更名中書謁者令爲中謁者令，初置尚書，員五人，有四丞。

translations.literal: In Jianshi 4 under Emperor Cheng, the Director of the Palace Secretary Ushers was renamed Director of the Palace Ushers, and the Masters of Documents were first established with a complement of five and four Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianshi 4 under Emperor Cheng, the Palace Secretary Ushers' Director was renamed Director of the Palace Ushers, and the Masters of Documents were formally established with five members and four Deputies.

sentences.zh: 河平元年省東織，更名西織爲織室。

translations.literal: In Heping 1, the Eastern Weaving office was abolished, and the Western Weaving was renamed the Weaving Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping 1, the Eastern Weaving office was abolished and the Western Weaving was renamed the Weaving Chamber.

sentences.zh: 綏和二年，哀帝省樂府。

translations.literal: In Suihe 2, Emperor Ai abolished the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Suihe 2, Emperor Ai abolished the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 王莽改少府曰共工。

translations.literal: Wang Mang renamed the Privy Treasurer to Minister of Shared Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang renamed the Privy Treasurer 'Minister of Shared Works.'

sentences.zh: 中尉，秦官，掌徼循京師，有兩丞、候、司馬、千人。

translations.literal: The Capital Commandant was a Qin office, responsible for patrolling the capital, with two Deputies, a Scout, a Marshal, and a Commander of a Thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Commandant was a Qin office in charge of patrolling the capital, with two Deputies, a Scout, a Marshal, and a Commander of a Thousand.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名執金吾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the title was changed to Bearer of the Golden Mace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the title was changed to Bearer of the Golden Mace.

sentences.zh: 屬官有中壘、寺互、武庫、都船四令丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included four Directors and Deputies: the Central Rampart, Temple Mutual, Arsenal, and Capital Boats.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included four Directors and Deputies: Central Rampart, Temple Mutual, Arsenal, and Capital Boats.

sentences.zh: 都船、武庫有三丞，中壘兩尉。

translations.literal: The Capital Boats and Arsenal each had three Deputies; the Central Rampart had two Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Boats and Arsenal each had three Deputies; the Central Rampart had two Commandants.

sentences.zh: 又式道左右中候、候丞及左右京輔都尉、尉丞兵卒皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Additionally, the Left, Right, and Central Scouts of the Ceremony Road and their Deputy Scouts, as well as the Left and Right Capital Adjunct Commandants and their Deputy Commandants and soldiers, all fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Left, Right, and Central Scouts of the Ceremony Road with their Deputies, and the Left and Right Capital Adjunct Commandants with their Deputies and soldiers, also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 初，寺互屬少府，中屬主爵，後屬中尉。

translations.literal: Originally, the Temple Mutual was under the Privy Treasurer, then transferred to the Director of Nobility Ranks, and later placed under the Capital Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, the Temple Mutual fell under the Privy Treasurer, then was transferred to the Director of Nobility Ranks, and later to the Capital Commandant.

sentences.zh: 自太常至執金吾，秩皆中二千石，丞皆千石。

translations.literal: From Grand Master of Ceremonies through Bearer of the Golden Mace, the rank was in all cases middle 2,000-shi; their Deputies were all 1,000-shi.
translations.idiomatic: From Grand Master of Ceremonies down to Bearer of the Golden Mace, all these offices were classified as middle 2,000-shi rank, and all their Deputies were 1,000-shi.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅、少傅，古官。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent were ancient offices.
translations.idiomatic: The posts of Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent were offices of ancient origin.

sentences.zh: 屬官有太子門大夫、庶子、先馬、舍人。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials included Gentlemen of the Heir Apparent's Gate, Attendants, Masters of Horses, and Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Their subordinate staff included Gentlemen of the Heir Apparent's Gate, Attendants, Masters of Horses, and Retainers.

sentences.zh: 將作少府，秦官，掌治宮室，有兩丞、左右中候。

translations.literal: The Junior Treasurer of Construction was a Qin office, responsible for managing palace buildings, with two Deputies and Left, Right, and Central Scouts.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Treasurer of Construction was a Qin office in charge of building the palaces, with two Deputies and Left, Right, and Central Scouts.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名將作大匠。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the title was changed to Grand Architect.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the title was changed to Grand Architect.

sentences.zh: 屬官有石庫、東園主章、左右前後中校七令丞，又主章長丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices included seven Directors and Deputies: Stone Repository, Eastern Garden Timber Master, and the Left, Right, Front, Rear, and Central School Commandants. There was also a Chief and Deputy of the Timber Master.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included seven Directors and Deputies — Stone Repository, Eastern Garden Timber Master, and the five School Commandants (Left, Right, Front, Rear, and Central). There was also a Timber Master Chief with Deputy.

sentences.zh: 武帝太初元年更名東園主章爲木工。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Eastern Garden Timber Master was renamed the Woodworkers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Eastern Garden Timber Master was renamed the Woodworkers' Bureau.

sentences.zh: 成帝陽朔三年省中候及左右前後中校五丞。

translations.literal: In Yangshuo 3 under Emperor Cheng, the Central Scout and the five Deputies of the Left, Right, Front, Rear, and Central Schools were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yangshuo 3 under Emperor Cheng, the Central Scout and the Deputies of the five Schools were abolished.

sentences.zh: 詹事，秦官，[85]掌皇后、太子家，有丞。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Household was a Qin office; it managed the Empress's and Heir Apparent's households, and had a Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Household was a Qin-era post overseeing the domestic establishments of the Empress and Crown Prince, with a Deputy attached.

sentences.zh: [86]屬官有太子率更、家令丞，僕、中盾、衞率、厨廄長丞，[87]又中長秋、私府、永巷、倉、廄、祠祀、食官令長丞。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials included the Heir Apparent's Prefect of Watches, Household Director and Deputy, Steward, Central Shield Guard, Guard Commandant, and the Chiefs and Deputies of kitchens and stables; also Directors, Chiefs, and Deputies of the Inner Chamberlain, Private Treasury, Yong Lane, granaries, stables, sacrificial services, and food offices.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices were extensive: they included the Crown Prince's Prefect of Watches, Household Director and Deputy, Steward, Central Shield Guard, Guard Commandant, and chiefs and deputies for kitchens and stables, as well as directors, chiefs, and deputies over the Inner Chamberlain's Office, the Private Treasury, Yong Lane, granaries, stables, ritual services, and food administration.

sentences.zh: 諸宦官皆屬焉。

translations.literal: All eunuch officials were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: All eunuch personnel fell under its authority.

sentences.zh: [88]成帝鴻嘉三年省詹事官，并屬大長秋。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's Hongjia third year, the Director of the Palace Household office was abolished and merged under the Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Cheng's Hongjia era, the Director of the Palace Household was abolished, and its functions were consolidated under the Grand Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: [89]長信詹事掌皇太后宮，景帝中六年更名長信少府，[90]平帝元始四年更名長樂少府。

translations.literal: The Changxin Director of the Palace Household managed the Empress Dowager's palace. In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year it was renamed Changxin Privy Treasurer; in Emperor Ping's Yuanshi fourth year it was renamed Changle Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The Changxin Director of the Palace Household administered the Empress Dowager's palace. In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year the title was changed to Changxin Privy Treasurer, and in Emperor Ping's fourth Yuanshi year it was changed again to Changle Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 將行，秦官，[91]景帝中六年更名大長秋，[92]或用中人，或用士人。

translations.literal: Palace Chamberlain was a Qin office. [91]In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year it was renamed Grand Chamberlain. [92]Sometimes eunuchs were appointed, sometimes scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Chamberlain was originally a Qin office. In Emperor Jing's sixth Zhong year it was renamed Grand Chamberlain. Appointments to it alternated between eunuchs and regular scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 典屬國，秦官，掌蠻夷降者。

translations.literal: The Director of Dependent States was a Qin office, responsible for the submitted barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Dependent States was a Qin office in charge of submitted barbarian peoples.

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩三年昆邪王降，復增屬國，置都尉、丞、候、千人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Kunxie King surrendered, additional dependent states were established, with Commandants, Deputies, Scouts, and Commanders of a Thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Kunxie King surrendered, additional dependent states were created, with Commandants, Deputies, Scouts, and Commanders of a Thousand.

sentences.zh: 屬官，九譯令。

translations.literal: The subordinate office was the Director of Nine Interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate office was the Director of Nine Interpreters.

sentences.zh: 成帝河平元年省并大鴻臚。

translations.literal: In Heping 1 under Emperor Cheng, the office was abolished and merged into the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping 1 under Emperor Cheng, the office was abolished and merged with the Grand Herald.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 93.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 93.

sentences.zh: 水衡都尉，[95]武帝元鼎二年初置，掌上林苑，有五丞。

translations.literal: The Superintendent of Waterways and Parks was first established in Emperor Wu's Yuanding second year; it managed the Shanglin Park and had five Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Superintendent of Waterways and Parks was first created in Emperor Wu's second Yuanding year. It oversaw Shanglin Park and had five Deputies.

sentences.zh: 屬官有上林、均輸、御羞、禁圃、輯濯、鍾官、技巧、六廄、辯銅九官令丞。

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices were Shanglin, Equitable Transport, Imperial Provisions, Forbidden Gardens, Cleansing and Washing, Bell Foundry, Craftsmanship, Six Stables, and Copper Assay - nine offices with Directors and Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate structure included nine bureaus - Shanglin, Equitable Transport, Imperial Provisions, Forbidden Gardens, Cleansing and Washing, Bell Foundry, Craftsmanship, the Six Stables, and Copper Assay - each staffed by Directors and Deputies.

sentences.zh: [96]又衡官、水司空、都水、農倉，又甘泉上林、都水七官長丞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: In addition, the Works Office, Water Minister of Works, Metropolitan Waterways, and Agricultural Granaries, and also the Ganquan Shanglin and Metropolitan Waterways offices - seven offices' Chiefs and Deputies - were all subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: It also controlled seven additional units - including the Works Office, Water Minister of Works, Metropolitan Waterways, Agricultural Granaries, and the Ganquan-Shanglin and Metropolitan Waterways branches - together with their chiefs and deputies.

sentences.zh: 上林有八丞十二尉，均輸四丞，御羞兩丞，都水三丞，禁圃兩尉，甘泉上林四丞。

translations.literal: Shanglin had eight Deputies and twelve Commandants; Equitable Transport had four Deputies; Imperial Provisions had two Deputies; Metropolitan Waterways had three Deputies; Forbidden Gardens had two Commandants; Ganquan Shanglin had four Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The staffing distribution was as follows: Shanglin had eight Deputies and twelve Commandants; Equitable Transport, four Deputies; Imperial Provisions, two Deputies; Metropolitan Waterways, three Deputies; Forbidden Gardens, two Commandants; and Ganquan Shanglin, four Deputies.

sentences.zh: 成帝建始二年省技巧、六廄官。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's Jianshi second year, the Craftsmanship and Six Stables offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Cheng's Jianshi era, the Craftsmanship and Six Stables bureaus were abolished.

sentences.zh: 王莽改水衡都尉曰予虞。

translations.literal: Wang Mang renamed the Superintendent of Waterways and Parks as Forester of Provision.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang changed the title of Superintendent of Waterways and Parks to Forester of Provision.

sentences.zh: 初，御羞、上林、衡官及鑄錢皆屬少府。

translations.literal: Originally, Imperial Provisions, Shanglin, the Works Office, and coin-casting all belonged to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Imperial Provisions, Shanglin, the Works Office, and minting operations were all under the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 內史，周官，秦因之，掌治京師。

translations.literal: The Internal Clerk was a Zhou office, continued by Qin, responsible for governing the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Internal Clerk was a Zhou office continued by the Qin, in charge of governing the capital.

sentences.zh: 景帝二年分置左內史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Jing, a Left Internal Clerk was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's second year, a Left Internal Clerk was established as a separate post.

sentences.zh: 右內史武帝太初元年更名京兆尹，屬官有長安市、厨兩令丞，又都水、鐵官兩長丞。

translations.literal: The Right Internal Clerk was renamed the Governor of the Capital Region in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu. Subordinate offices included two Directors and Deputies: the Chang'an Market and Kitchen, as well as two Chiefs and Deputies: Capital Water and Iron Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, the Right Internal Clerk was renamed Governor of the Capital Region. Its subordinate offices included the Chang'an Market and Kitchen Directors and Deputies, and the Capital Water and Iron Office Chiefs and Deputies.

sentences.zh: 左內史更名左馮翊，屬官有廩犧令丞尉。

translations.literal: The Left Internal Clerk was renamed the Left Adjunct. Its subordinate offices included the Director, Deputy, and Commandant of the Granary Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Internal Clerk was renamed the Left Adjunct. Its subordinate offices included the Director, Deputy, and Commandant of the Granary Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又左都水、鐵官、雲壘、長安四市四長丞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Also the Left Capital Water, Iron Office, Cloud Rampart, and the Four Markets of Chang'an — four Chiefs and Deputies — all fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Capital Water, Iron Office, Cloud Rampart, and Four Markets of Chang'an — each with Chief and Deputy — also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 主爵中尉，秦官，掌列侯。

translations.literal: The Central Commandant of Nobility Ranks was a Qin office, responsible for the ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Commandant of Nobility Ranks was a Qin office in charge of the ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年更名都尉，武帝太初元年更名右扶風，治內史右地。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, the title was changed to Commandant. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it was renamed Right Adjunct, governing the right territory of the former Internal Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Jing's sixth middle year, it was renamed Commandant. In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu, it became the Right Adjunct, governing the right portion of the former Internal Clerk's territory.

sentences.zh: 屬官有掌畜令丞。

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices included the Director and Deputy of Livestock Management.
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate offices included the Director and Deputy of Livestock Management.

sentences.zh: 又有都水、鐵官、廄、廱厨四長丞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Also the Capital Water, Iron Office, Stables, and Yong Kitchen — four Chiefs and Deputies — all fell under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Water, Iron Office, Stables, and Yong Kitchen, each with Chief and Deputy, also fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 與左馮翊、京兆尹是爲三輔，皆有兩丞。

translations.literal: Together with the Left Adjunct and the Governor of the Capital Region, these constituted the Three Adjuncts, each with two Deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Left Adjunct and the Governor of the Capital Region, these formed the Three Adjuncts. Each had two Deputies.

sentences.zh: 列侯更屬大鴻臚。

translations.literal: The ranked marquises were subsequently placed under the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: The ranked marquises were later transferred to the Grand Herald's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 元鼎四年更置三輔都尉、都尉丞各一人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanding, Three Adjunct Commandants and one Deputy Commandant each were additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanding, Three Adjunct Commandants with one Deputy each were additionally established.

sentences.zh: 自太子太傅至右扶風，皆秩二千石，丞六百石。

translations.literal: From Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent down to Right Adjunct, all were rank 2,000-shi; Deputies were 600-shi.
translations.idiomatic: From Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent through Right Adjunct, all these posts carried 2,000-shi rank, with Deputies at 600-shi.

sentences.zh: 護軍都尉，秦官，武帝元狩四年屬大司馬，成帝綏和元年居大司馬府比司直，哀帝元壽元年更名司冦，平帝元始元年更名護軍。

translations.literal: The Protector-General Commandant was a Qin office. In the fourth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, it was placed under the Grand Marshal. In Suihe 1 under Emperor Cheng, it was stationed in the Grand Marshal's office at a rank equivalent to the Rectifier. In the first year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai, it was renamed Minister of Crime. In Yuanshi 1 under Emperor Ping, it was renamed Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The Protector-General Commandant was a Qin office. In the fourth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu it was placed under the Grand Marshal. In Suihe 1 under Emperor Cheng it was stationed in the Grand Marshal's office at Rectifier-equivalent rank. In the first year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai it was renamed Minister of Crime, and in Yuanshi 1 under Emperor Ping it became Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 司隷校尉，周官，武帝征和四年初置。

translations.literal: Director of Retainers was a Zhou office; it was first established in Emperor Wu's Zhenghe fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Retainers was an office of Zhou origin, first instituted in Emperor Wu's fourth Zhenghe year.

sentences.zh: 持節，從中都官徒千二百人，捕巫蠱，督大姦猾。

translations.literal: Holding a tally, it was accompanied by 1,200 convict laborers from central offices, to arrest witchcraft and gu-poisoning offenders and to supervise major criminals and the crafty.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a tally of authority and accompanied by 1,200 convict laborers from the central bureaus, it was charged with suppressing witchcraft and gu-poisoning cases and policing major criminals and the unscrupulous.

sentences.zh: 後罷其兵。

translations.literal: Later its troops were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Its military contingent was later disbanded.

sentences.zh: 察三輔、三河、弘農。

translations.literal: It inspected the Three Adjunct Regions, the Three River regions, and Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Its inspection jurisdiction covered the Three Adjuncts, the Three River regions, and Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 元帝初元四年去節。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's Chuyuan fourth year, the tally was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Yuan's Chuyuan era, the office's tally authority was revoked.

sentences.zh: 成帝元延四年省。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's Yuanyan fourth year, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The office was abolished in the fourth year of Emperor Cheng's Yuanyan era.

sentences.zh: 綏和二年，哀帝復置，但為司隷，冠進賢冠，屬大司空，比司直。

translations.literal: In Suihe second year, Emperor Ai restored it, but only as Director of Retainers; he wore the Jinxian cap, belonged under the Grand Minister of Works, and ranked equivalent to a Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Suihe, Emperor Ai restored the post, but only in the form of Director of Retainers. The officeholder wore the Jinxian cap, was subordinated to the Grand Minister of Works, and held rank equivalent to a Director.

sentences.zh: 城門校尉掌京師城門屯兵，有司馬、十二城門候。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the City Gates managed garrison troops at the capital's gates; there were a Marshal and twelve gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of the City Gates commanded the garrison forces posted at the capital gates, assisted by one Marshal and twelve gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 中壘校尉掌北軍壘門內，外掌西域。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Central Ramparts managed matters within the gate of the Northern Army barracks; externally he managed the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of the Central Ramparts oversaw affairs inside the gate of the Northern Army encampment, and beyond the capital handled matters of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉掌騎士。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Garrison Cavalry managed cavalry troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Garrison Cavalry commanded mounted troops.

sentences.zh: 步兵校尉掌上林苑門屯兵。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Infantry managed garrison troops at the gates of Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Infantry oversaw the garrison units stationed at the gates of Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉掌越騎。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Yue Cavalry managed the Yue cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Yue Cavalry commanded the Yue cavalry contingent.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉掌長水宣曲胡騎。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Changshui managed the Hu cavalry of Changshui and Xuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Changshui commanded the Hu cavalry units stationed at Changshui and Xuanqu.

sentences.zh: 又有胡騎校尉，掌池陽胡騎，不常置。

translations.literal: There was also a Colonel of Hu Cavalry, managing the Chiyang Hu cavalry, but it was not a permanent post.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Colonel of Hu Cavalry in charge of the Chiyang Hu cavalry, though the office was not maintained on a permanent basis.

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉掌待詔射聲士。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Archers managed the archers on imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Archers oversaw the archer-corps personnel serving under imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 虎賁校尉掌輕車。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Tiger Guards managed light chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of Tiger Guards commanded the light-chariot force.

sentences.zh: 凡八校尉，皆武帝初置，有丞、司馬。

translations.literal: In total there were eight colonels; all were first established under Emperor Wu, each with Deputies and Marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether there were eight such colonelcies, all first created in Emperor Wu's reign, each with its own Deputy and Marshal.

translations.literal: Annotation marker 115.
translations.idiomatic: Textual annotation marker 115.

sentences.zh: 自司隷至虎賁校尉，秩皆二千石。

translations.literal: From Director of Retainers through Colonel of Tiger Guards, all held rank 2,000-shi.
translations.idiomatic: All offices from Director of Retainers down to Colonel of Tiger Guards were set at 2,000-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 西域都護加官，宣帝地節二年初置，以騎都尉、諫大夫使護西域三十六國，有副校尉，秩比二千石，丞一人，司馬、候、千人各二人。

translations.literal: The Protector-General of the Western Regions was an additional office, first established in Emperor Xuan's Dijie second year. A Cavalry Commandant and a Remonstrant Grandee were dispatched to protect the thirty-six states of the Western Regions. There was a Deputy Colonel, rank equivalent to 2,000-shi, one Deputy, and two each of Marshals, wardens, and commanders of 1,000 men.
translations.idiomatic: The Protector-General of the Western Regions was an added office, first instituted in the second year of Emperor Xuan's Dijie era. A Cavalry Commandant and a Remonstrant Grandee were sent to oversee and protect the thirty-six states of the Western Regions. The organization included a Deputy Colonel at rank equivalent to 2,000-shi, one Deputy, and two each of Marshals, wardens, and thousand-man commanders.

sentences.zh: 戊己校尉，元帝初元元年置，有丞、司馬各一人，候五人，秩比六百石。

translations.literal: The Wuji Colonel was established in Emperor Yuan's Chuyuan first year; it had one Deputy, one Marshal, and five wardens, with rank equivalent to 600-shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuji Colonel was created in the first year of Emperor Yuan's Chuyuan era. Its staff comprised one Deputy, one Marshal, and five wardens, at rank equivalent to 600-shi.

sentences.zh: 奉軍都尉掌御乘輿車，駙馬都尉掌駙馬，皆武帝初置，秩比二千石。

translations.literal: The Fengjun Commandant managed the imperial carriage; the Imperial Son-in-law Commandant managed the imperial sons-in-law. Both were first established under Emperor Wu, with rank equivalent to 2,000-shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengjun Commandant oversaw the imperial carriage, while the Imperial Son-in-law Commandant oversaw the imperial sons-in-law. Both posts were first created in Emperor Wu's reign and carried rank equivalent to 2,000-shi.

sentences.zh: 侍中、左右曹、諸吏、散騎、中常侍，皆加官，所加或列侯、將軍、卿大夫、將、都尉、尚書、太醫、太官令至郎中，亡員，多至數十人。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left and Right Sections, Various Clerks, Loose Cavalry, and Regular Palace Attendant were all additional appointments. Those given these might be Marquises, Generals, High Ministers, Commanders, Commandants, Secretariat officials, Grand Physicians, Director of Grand Provisioning, down to Palace Gentlemen; there was no fixed number, often reaching several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: The titles Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left and Right Section official, Various Clerk, Loose Cavalry, and Regular Palace Attendant were all concurrent appointments. They could be conferred on men ranging from marquises and generals to high ministers, commandants, secretariat officials, grand physicians, provisioning directors, and even palace gentlemen. There was no fixed quota, and their number could run into the dozens.

sentences.zh: 侍中、中常侍得入禁中，諸曹受尚書事，諸吏得舉法，散騎騎並乘輿車。

translations.literal: Attendants-in-Ordinary and Regular Palace Attendants were permitted to enter the inner palace; the various sections handled Secretariat affairs; Various Clerks could raise legal measures; Loose Cavalry rode alongside the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants-in-Ordinary and Regular Palace Attendants were allowed access to the inner palace. The section officials handled secretariat business; the Various Clerks could initiate legal proceedings; and the Loose Cavalry rode in attendance beside the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 給事中亦加官，所加或大夫、博士、議郎，掌顧問應對，位次中常侍。

translations.literal: Attendant in Ordinary Service was also a concurrent appointment. Those appointed might be Grandees, Erudites, or Consulting Gentlemen; they managed consultation and response, with rank next to Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The post Attendant in Ordinary Service was likewise a concurrent title, typically conferred on grandees, erudites, or consulting gentlemen. Its function was court consultation and formal reply, and its precedence stood just below the Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 中黃門有給事黃門，位從將大夫。

translations.literal: Among the Palace Yellow Gate there were Yellow Gate Attendants in Service, whose rank followed that of General-Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Palace Yellow Gate staff were Yellow Gate Attendants in Service, ranked comparably to general-grandees.

sentences.zh: 皆秦制。

translations.literal: All these were Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: All of these followed Qin institutional precedent.

sentences.zh: 爵：一級曰公士，二上造，三簪裊，四不更，五大夫，六官大夫，七公大夫，八公乘，九五大夫，十左庶長，十一右庶長，十二左更，十三中更，十四右更，十五少上造，十六大上造，十七駟車庶長，十八大庶長，十九關內侯，二十徹侯。
